diagnostics.message: `:resource.aws_config_configuration_aggregator.organization` is created with `organization_aggregation_source.role_arn` from `aws_iam_role.config_organization`, so it only waits for the role itself. The aggregator immediately assumes that role to read AWS Organizations, which requires AWSConfigRoleForOrganizations to be attached first (the provider's own organization-aggregator example uses `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.organization]`). `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.config_organization` is a sibling with no ordering relative to the aggregator, so creation can fail with an insufficient-permissions error.

`:module.config_baseline_ap-northeast-1` (and every other `config_baseline_*` region module) only receives `s3_bucket_name = local.audit_log_bucket_id`, which depends on the bucket itself, not on its policy. Enabling the recorder validates that AWS Config can access the audit bucket (`s3:GetBucketAcl`/`s3:PutObject` are granted by `:resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.audit_log`), so `aws_config_delivery_channel.bucket` / `aws_config_configuration_recorder_status.recorder` can race ahead of the bucket policy and fail with InsufficientDeliveryPolicyException. This is the same external ordering the CloudTrail module needs (it uses the `cloudtrail_depends_on` variable hack for exactly this bucket policy); the config modules have no equivalent.

`module.cloudtrail_baseline:resource.aws_cloudtrail.global` passes `sns_topic_name` from `aws_sns_topic.cloudtrail-sns-topic`, but nothing orders it after `module.cloudtrail_baseline:resource.aws_sns_topic_policy.local-account-cloudtrail`, which is what grants `cloudtrail.amazonaws.com` permission to publish to that topic. Creating the trail before the topic policy exists fails with an invalid / insufficient SNS-topic-policy error. The module's `depends_on` via `var.cloudtrail_depends_on` only covers the S3 bucket policy, not the topic policy.
